scope: Batch review of C08, E01, E02, E03, E04 only, by code reading; nothing was run. Inventory (brace-inventory.json) and prescan (brace-prescan.json) were read. Read: app/ (audit, loop, extractor, context_size, identity, mcp_client, startup, main, gate, settings, tools/), migrations, release/manifest.yaml, config/, deploy/k8s, Dockerfile, pyproject.toml, CI workflow, README. Not found: any .brace/ record, dependency inventory, lockfile, vulnerability scan, retention/TTL config, tool-quarantine control. findings.title: Connect configuration to execution
findings.requirement: From a trace, look up the release manifest, the context sizes at each decision, and any prompts a parent passed to a sub-agent. Keep these links for the full audit retention period. Control access to sensitive artifacts.

not_covered.problem: Context size not measured or logged for each action decision
Action records missing any of the six identity fields
Manifest missing components that define the release

evidence.note: Every audit row carries agent_type_id (audit.py:103, NOT NULL in migrations). But the value is a hash computed at startup over the manifest; no stored manifest is keyed by it. release/manifest.yaml has no agent_type_id field and nothing writes the manifest to a store under that key. startup.py:43 only logs when running state differs from the manifest, so the id can describe a manifest the process is not running.

checks.check: Each trace or audit record carries the agent-type-id or manifest reference that resolves to the stored release manifest.
checks.verify: 1) Open the trace or audit record writer. 2) Check every record carries `agent.type.id` or a manifest reference. 3) Check that value is the key of a stored manifest. 4) Answer no if the field is missing on some paths (errors, background jobs) or holds a value that resolves to no stored manifest.
checks.counter_search: Searched app/, release/, migrations/, .github/ for a manifest store, registry, table or file keyed by agent_type_id / atid; found none.
checks.note: Every audit row carries agent_type_id (audit.py:103, NOT NULL in migrations). But the value is a hash computed at startup over the manifest; no stored manifest is keyed by it. release/manifest.yaml has no agent_type_id field and nothing writes the manifest to a store under that key. startup.py:43 only logs when running state differs from the manifest, so the id can describe a manifest the process is not running.

checks.check: The context size at each model decision is recorded in the trace.
checks.verify: 1) Find model call sites and their spans. 2) Look for the context size recorded per call (for example `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` or a context-length attribute). 3) Answer no if it is missing on any model call path, including retries and sub-agents.
checks.counter_search: Searched all messages.create/count_tokens uses in app/: only loop.py:150 and extractor.py:74 call the model; both are preceded by measure_context and recorded on model_decision rows. No other client calls found.
checks.note: Context size counted before each call and finalized from usage; stored in context_tokens/context_method on the model_decision audit row for parent and sub-agent.

coverage.subject: I11d074af40
coverage.note: Main-agent model call: context counted before the call, finalized from usage after (loop.py:153) and written on the model_decision row (loop.py:154-155).

coverage.subject: I1bba76f5cb

checks.check: Prompts passed from a parent to a sub-agent are stored and linked from the trace.
checks.verify: 1) Find sub-agent spawn code. 2) Check the parent's prompt is stored and the trace holds a link to it (ID, hash, or URI). 3) Answer no if the prompt is not stored, prompt capture is off, or the trace has no link.
checks.counter_search: Searched app/ and deploy/ for any store of the parent-to-child prompt text (prompt table, blob, URI); found none.
checks.note: The sub-agent start row stores only doc_id and the parent's span id as parent_prompt_ref. The task text built at extractor.py:46 is not stored, and the system prompt is not stored either; run_started stores only task_sha256 (loop.py:135). OTEL message-content capture is set to false in deploy/k8s/deployment.yaml:67.

checks.check: Storage config keeps manifests, traces, and these links for at least the audit retention period, and limits access to sensitive artifacts by role.
checks.verify: 1) Find storage config for manifests, traces, and prompt links: bucket lifecycle rules, log retention, TTLs. 2) Check retention covers the audit period for all of them. 3) Check IAM limits sensitive artifacts by role. 4) Answer no if any has a shorter TTL, no retention, or broad read access. Answer unknown if storage is configured outside this repo.
checks.quote: GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON audit_events TO procurement_agent;
checks.note: Agent role is insert-only on audit_events and ops can SELECT (001_init.sql:132), but the repo has no retention, TTL, lifecycle or partition policy for manifests, traces or audit rows, and no audit retention period. OTLP traces go to an external collector (deployment.yaml:63). Storage config appears to live outside this repo.

findings.summary: Audit rows carry a hashed agent_type_id that resolves to no stored manifest, and the parent's prompt to the extractor sub-agent is not stored.
findings.next_step: Store each release manifest keyed by agent_type_id, store the parent-to-sub-agent prompt (or its content-addressed copy) with a link in the audit row, and confirm audit retention outside this repo.

Using an upstream service doesn't make its controls N/A.

A vendor service dropping agent or tenant identity from its records

findings.title: Vet and pin dependencies
findings.requirement: Before approving a tool or server, review its source code or available provenance, publisher, permissions, update path, and known vulnerabilities. Include model files, adapters, and datasets. Pin versions or digests, and verify signatures where they exist. A registry's namespace check shows who controls a publisher account, not that the code is safe. Record the limits of remote services and unsigned artifacts, and the extra checks you use instead.

not_covered.problem: A tool's description or schema changing after it was approved
Hidden instructions inside a tool's metadata
Lookalike or duplicate tool names across servers
Container image not pinned by digest or signature-checked

evidence.note: Direct dependencies are == pinned (pyproject.toml:7-17) and images are digest pinned, but there is no lockfile or hash file, so transitive packages resolve floating at build time, and there is no [build-system] pin. The ERP MCP server is pinned only by tool metadata fingerprints; no implementation version or digest is recorded.

checks.check: Each tool, MCP server, package, model file, adapter, and dataset is pinned by exact version or digest, with no floating tags, ranges, or 'latest'.
checks.verify: 1) Open lockfiles, `*.mcp.json`, Dockerfiles, and model or dataset download code. 2) Check each tool, MCP server, package, model file, adapter, and dataset uses an exact version or digest. 3) Answer no if any uses a range, `latest`, a branch, `npx` or `uvx` without a version, or an unpinned download URL.
checks.counter_search: Searched for requirements*.txt, *.lock, constraints, --require-hashes, *.mcp.json; none exist.
checks.note: Direct dependencies are == pinned (pyproject.toml:7-17) and images are digest pinned, but there is no lockfile or hash file, so transitive packages resolve floating at build time, and there is no [build-system] pin. The ERP MCP server is pinned only by tool metadata fingerprints; no implementation version or digest is recorded.

checks.check: Signature checks run in the build or load path where the publisher provides signatures, and a failed check stops the install or load.
checks.verify: 1) Find install and load steps in CI and code. 2) Check signature checks (`cosign verify`, `npm audit signatures`, sigstore, GPG) run where the publisher signs. 3) Answer no if a check is missing, its failure is ignored (`|| true`, `continue-on-error`, `try/except` that continues), or a second install path skips it.
checks.note: The release signs its own image and Kyverno verifies it. No CI step verifies a third-party signature (distroless base image, PyPI attestations); base-image signature checking belongs to B10. Whether each publisher signs is not determinable from the repo.

checks.check: A vulnerability scan of the pinned dependency list runs in CI and gates on the team's release policy.
checks.verify: 1) Open CI workflows. 2) Find a vulnerability scan (`pip-audit`, `npm audit`, `osv-scanner`, `trivy`, `grype`) of the pinned dependency list. 3) Check it fails the build per the release policy. 4) Answer no if no scan exists, it is set not to fail (`--exit-zero`, `|| true`, `continue-on-error`), or it scans a different file than the lockfile actually used.
checks.counter_search: Searched .github/workflows/ci.yaml for pip-audit, osv, trivy, grype, dependabot, audit; none present.
checks.note: CI runs pytest, a gitleaks secret scan and a manifest hash check. No pip-audit, osv-scanner, trivy or grype step scans the dependency list or image for vulnerabilities, and nothing gates on findings.

checks.check: Each approved dependency's record names its publisher, permissions, and update source, and remote services or unsigned artifacts have a recorded exception.
checks.verify: 1) Find the dependency approval records. 2) Check each names publisher, permissions, and update source. 3) Check each remote service and unsigned artifact has a recorded exception. 4) Answer no if any approved dependency lacks these fields or the needed exception.
checks.counter_search: Searched repo for dependency review/approval/exception records; none found.
checks.note: Models list provider and snapshot source, but there are no approval records naming publisher, permissions and update source for packages, the ERP MCP server or base images, and no recorded exceptions for the remote services (ERP gateway, Anthropic API) or unsigned artifacts.

findings.summary: No vulnerability scan runs in CI, transitive packages are unpinned, and no dependency approval records exist.
findings.next_step: Add a lockfile with hashes, a gating pip-audit or osv-scanner step in CI, and per-dependency approval records with publisher, permissions, update source and exceptions.

findings.title: Re-check tools on load
findings.requirement: Keep a tool publication lifecycle: discovery, review, approval, enablement, re-check, quarantine, and rollback. New servers and tools start disabled; their owner approves descriptions, schemas, permissions, and implementation references before use. Take a fingerprint of each approved tool's description and schema. Compare it whenever the tool loads, its cache refreshes, or its tool list changes. Block unexpected changes until reviewed, including when re-checking fails; don't serve a cached definition as a fallback. Record the policy/config version used at execution, bound propagation delay, and test rollback without restoring revoked access. A metadata hash cannot detect hidden changes to remote code. Pin or attest implementations where visible, record remote visibility limits and review dates, and track affected deployments when vulnerabilities are reported.

not_covered.problem: Hidden instructions in a tool's metadata when first approved
Tool approved without reviewing its publisher and permissions
A new server quietly swapping its tool in for an approved one
Cached tool list shared across authorization contexts

evidence.note: At startup an unpinned tool raises (mcp_client.py:95-98), but on a list_changed notice refresh_tools() accepts every tool the server returns with no pin lookup, so new tools are enabled on discovery. Pins in release/manifest.yaml:70-81 cover name, description, inputSchema and annotations only; title, outputSchema, permissions and implementation reference are not in the fingerprint (mcp_client.py:43-48). Owner approval of the pins is not visible in the repo.

checks.check: New tools start disabled, an owner approves versioned definitions and grants before enablement, and approved descriptions/schemas have stored fingerprints.
checks.verify: 1) Trace discovery, approval and enablement on startup and dynamic registration. 2) Check the owner-approved version includes permissions and implementation references and has a stored description/schema hash. 3) Reject auto-enable on discovery, self-approval from untrusted metadata, or fingerprints covering only names. 4) Use unknown for approval service behavior not visible in this repo.
checks.quote: self._tools = {t["name"]: t for t in tools}
checks.counter_search: Searched app/ for a disabled/quarantine/approved state on discovered tools; none.
checks.note: At startup an unpinned tool raises (mcp_client.py:95-98), but on a list_changed notice refresh_tools() accepts every tool the server returns with no pin lookup, so new tools are enabled on discovery. Pins in release/manifest.yaml:70-81 cover name, description, inputSchema and annotations only; title, outputSchema, permissions and implementation reference are not in the fingerprint (mcp_client.py:43-48). Owner approval of the pins is not visible in the repo.

checks.check: The fingerprint is re-checked on every tool load, cache refresh, and list-changed notice from the server.
checks.verify: 1) List every path that loads tool definitions: startup, cache refresh, reconnect, and the `notifications/tools/list_changed` handler. 2) Check each recomputes the fingerprint and compares it with the stored one. 3) Answer no if any path skips the compare, or both sides of the compare are computed from the new definition.
checks.counter_search: Searched for other loaders of tool definitions (reconnect, cache refresh): refresh_tools and initialize are the only ones; refresh_tools skips the compare.
checks.note: Startup (mcp_client.py:94-98) compares each fingerprint to the manifest pin. The list_changed handler calls refresh_tools (lines 105, 107-111), which replaces self._tools with no fingerprint compare and no scan. No other reload path found.

checks.check: When the re-check fails, the tool is blocked and the cached definition is not used.
checks.verify: 1) Open the fingerprint mismatch branch. 2) Check it blocks the tool and does not fall back to the cached definition. 3) Answer no if it only logs, uses the cached or new definition anyway, or an error during the check lets the tool load.
checks.quote: self._tools = {t["name"]: t for t in tools}
checks.counter_search: Looked for any block or rollback on the refresh path; none.
checks.note: The mismatch branch at startup raises (mcp_client.py:98) and blocks the tool. After a list_changed refresh there is no mismatch branch: changed or new definitions replace the approved ones and call() (line 117) accepts any name in the refreshed map.

checks.check: The implementation version is pinned or attested where it can be seen, and recorded separately from the metadata fingerprint.
checks.verify: 1) Check how each tool server implementation is referenced: package version, image digest, or attestation. 2) Check that version is recorded in its own field, apart from the metadata fingerprint. 3) Answer no if a visible implementation is unpinned, or only the metadata hash is recorded.
checks.note: The ERP MCP server is a remote gateway (manifest.yaml:65). The manifest records its endpoint and owner and metadata pins only; no implementation version, image digest or attestation field exists, and the server code is not visible here. Remote visibility limits and review dates are not recorded.

checks.check: Tool quarantine, bounded config propagation, recorded execution config versions, and rollback preserve revocations.
checks.verify: 1) Trace control-plane config to all executors, caches and reload paths. 2) Check a propagation bound and version in execution records. 3) Verify quarantine blocks calls and rollback cannot resurrect revoked grants. 4) Answer no for stale permissions surviving the bound or unsafe rollback; use unknown for runtime guarantees lacking evidence.
checks.counter_search: Searched app/ and config/ for quarantine, disable, revoke, rollback, propagation; none for tools.
checks.note: The only stop control is a fleet or tenant halt of whole runs. There is no per-tool or per-server quarantine, no propagation bound for tool or policy config, and no rollback logic that preserves revocations. policy_version is recorded on authz rows (loop.py:70) but tool-set version is not.

violates: Compare it whenever the tool loads, its cache refreshes, or its tool list changes
findings.summary: The list_changed refresh path replaces tool definitions with no fingerprint compare, scan or block, and no tool quarantine or rollback exists; no code calls the handler yet, so this is latent.
findings.next_step: Make refresh_tools reuse the startup pin check and scan, fail closed without falling back to cached definitions, add a per-tool quarantine, and record implementation versions separately.

findings.title: Inspect tool metadata
findings.requirement: Before the model sees them, scan server instructions, tool names, titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, annotations, and prompt and resource templates. Look for hidden instructions, references to other servers' tools, invisible or control characters, role overrides, encoded payloads, and places data could be sent. Limit lengths, and clean or reject anything suspicious. Check that a scanner error doesn't quietly let unchecked metadata through.

not_covered.problem: A tool's description or schema changing after it was approved
Hidden instructions in tool call results
Lookalike or duplicate tool names across servers
Allow decisions based on server hints such as read-only

evidence.note: scan_metadata runs only inside initialize() (line 99) over json.dumps of the whole tool dict. refresh_tools (lines 107-111) loads definitions with no scan. Server instructions, prompt templates and resource templates are never fetched or scanned. Field matrix: names, titles, descriptions, schemas and annotations are scanned at startup only; the data_sending_targets rule exists for no field. The model sees only in-house tool schemas (app/tools/erp.py:57-106), so MCP metadata is not currently model-visible.

checks.check: A scanner runs on server instructions, tool names, titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, annotations, and prompt and resource templates before the model sees them.
checks.verify: 1) Inventory every model-visible metadata field and loading path. 2) Build a field-by-rule matrix: names, titles, descriptions, schemas, annotations, instructions, prompts and resource templates. 3) For each field, trace the actual scanner rules applied before serialization to the model. A syntax regex alone is not proof that payload/instruction rules ran. 4) Try the same suspicious string in different fields; answer no for an unscanned required surface.
checks.quote: self._tools = {t["name"]: t for t in tools}
checks.counter_search: Searched app/ for other scan or sanitize calls on tool metadata; only mcp_client.py:99.
checks.note: scan_metadata runs only inside initialize() (line 99) over json.dumps of the whole tool dict. refresh_tools (lines 107-111) loads definitions with no scan. Server instructions, prompt templates and resource templates are never fetched or scanned. Field matrix: names, titles, descriptions, schemas and annotations are scanned at startup only; the data_sending_targets rule exists for no field. The model sees only in-house tool schemas (app/tools/erp.py:57-106), so MCP metadata is not currently model-visible.

checks.check: The scanner checks for hidden instructions, references to other servers' tools, invisible or control characters, role overrides, encoded payloads, and data-sending targets, and enforces length limits.
checks.verify: 1) Trace rule application, not just rule declarations. 2) Attempt encoded strings and multi-line role overrides; record input, exact code path and outcome. 3) Verify hidden instructions, cross-tool references, control/invisible characters, role overrides, encoded payloads, data-sending targets and length limits. 4) Answer no when a required rule is absent or a demonstrated suspicious input bypasses it.
checks.counter_search: Traced scan_metadata (lines 53-60) against the two inputs above; both reach 'self._tools' unflagged.
checks.note: Rules: ignore-instructions phrase, 'system prompt|you are now|act as', before/instead of calling x.y, invisible chars, base64 of 120+ chars. No rule for data-sending targets (URLs, emails, webhooks). Role overrides and cross-tool references are narrow. Multiline: json.dumps turns a newline into a literal backslash-n, so 'ignore\nall instructions' does not match the single-space 'ignore (all|any|previous|prior) instructions' pattern. Encoded: base64 under 120 chars, hex or URL-encoded payloads pass. Length limit covers description only (line 55).

checks.check: Metadata the scanner flags is cleaned or rejected, not just logged.
checks.verify: 1) Open the scanner's result handling. 2) Check flagged metadata is cleaned, or the tool rejected, before the model sees it. 3) Answer no if flagged items are only logged or warned about and passed through.
checks.counter_search: Searched mcp_client.py for log-only branches on scanner results; the only handling of a match is the raise.
checks.note: A flagged tool aborts initialize() before the tool map is set. Scope: scanner results at startup only; the refresh path never calls the scanner (see E04.1).

coverage.subject: scan_metadata result in initialize
coverage.note: A flagged tool raises; initialize() (mcp_client.py:99) propagates it before self._tools is assigned (line 100), so startup stops and the tool is rejected, not logged.

coverage.subject: overlong description
coverage.note: Length violations also reject rather than truncate or log.

checks.check: A scanner error or outage blocks the metadata instead of letting it through unchecked.
checks.verify: 1) Read every `try/except`, `catch`, and timeout around the scanner call. 2) Check an error blocks the metadata. 3) Answer no if any error branch passes metadata through, returns clean, or skips the scan, or a config flag disables scanning by default.
checks.counter_search: Searched app/ for try/except or flags around scan_metadata; none, so errors propagate and abort startup.
checks.note: Scanner errors fail closed at startup. Scope: scanner errors only; the missing scan on refresh is recorded under E04.1.

coverage.subject: scanner call in initialize
coverage.note: scan_metadata has no try/except and no disable flag; any error (including from json.dumps) propagates out of initialize() and aborts startup before self._tools is set.

coverage.subject: scan_metadata body
coverage.note: No exception is caught around the pattern loop (mcp_client.py:58-60), so an error cannot return clean.

findings.summary: The scanner has no data-sending-target rule, narrow hidden-instruction and override patterns, and never runs on refreshed tool lists.
findings.next_step: Add rules for data-sending targets, cross-tool references and role overrides that survive newlines, scan every load path and every metadata field, and add fixtures for each rule.
